item.title: Georgia vs. Ole Miss: Playoff stakes are high in this emerging SEC rivalry
item.description: The College Football Playoff has altered the trajectory of the sport in so many ways, and the 24-team bracket will cause even more chaos . But one immediate benefit is that the CFP creates instant blood rivalries; there’s nothing quite like the prospect of ending another team’s season to fire up the blood. Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2 SEC) and Georgia (7-1, 5-1 SEC), which meet this weekend in a crucial SEC game, last lined up against one another on the first day of 2026 in the Sugar Bowl, and what resulted was an absolutely spectacular, 14-score game that was in doubt until literally the final seconds of the game. Ole Miss won, 39-34, but only after Georgia had tied the game with 56 seconds remaining. The stakes when these two teams meet on Saturday in Oxford aren’t quite so existential, but close. Georgia, ranked No. 2 in the initial CFP rankings, should be fine to make the playoff even with a loss, but Ole Miss, at No. 10, could be in trouble. Whoever wins gets an easier path to the SEC championship and its coveted first-round bye. At this point in the season, everyone knows what’s what, and it’s just a matter of executing. And for both teams, it’s a matter of containment — for Ole Miss, containing Georgia’s run game; for Georgia, containing Ole Miss’ do-everything quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. Trinidad Chambliss will be the key to Ole Miss' chances of upsetting Georgia on Saturday. Justin Ford via Getty Images Kirby Smart, in the midst of his usual glossing of the next week’s opponent, lasered in on what makes Chambliss so difficult to defend against. “It's not the ‘wow!’ plays. The wow plays are what you guys love and what America loves,” he told assembled media earlier this week. “It's the down-in, down-out decision making that he's really elite at. The accuracy that he's elite at, the release, the decision. His pinpointing. He has an anticipation of windows that's probably unmatched. … He goes forwards, backwards as fast as he goes sideways.” Chambliss, to Smart’s mind, presents a unique challenge because of his talent, his experience, and his system under head coach Pete Golding. “There's nothing we're going to do that he hasn't seen,” Smart said. “You're not tricking the guy. I think that's what people get infatuated with, is, ‘How can I trick him and do that?’ You can't do that. … There's not a perfect remedy. If there was, somebody would have done it.” The Rebels are averaging 282.1 yards through the air this season, second only to LSU in the SEC. Georgia’s defense ranks sixth in the conference, giving up 186.6 yards through the air per game. item.title: Browns injuries: Deshaun Watson update as 2 of 4 starters return to practice
item.description: As the Cleveland Browns prepare for the New Orleans Saints, the official injury reports each day look like they will provide a lot of information about how Week 9 will go. On Wednesday, the Browns announced that QB Deshaun Watson was in concussion protocol , with QB Shedeur Sanders likely to start in his place . Along with Watson, four Cleveland starters missed the first practice of the wee k. On the other side, the Saints saw WR Jordyn Tyson and OT Kelvin Banks Jr. return to practice with a chance to return from injured reserve this week. On Thursday, Watson was not at practice, and DT Maliek Collins was still sidelined, but OT Austin Barber and LB Quincy Williams returned to the practice field in Berea. Some good news for Cleveland’s chances in Week 9, but Collins is a big part of the team’s defensive line. item.title: Max Verstappen jokes about rain threat in Brazil: "I've installed antivirus now!"
item.description: Motorsport photo The first wet race with Formula 1’s 2026 cars did not exactly prove to be a resounding success. During the formation laps behind the safety car at the Sepang International Circuit, almost half the field came to a halt. The issue turned out to be a software bug linked to the 250kW restrictions imposed by the FIA for wet-weather races. That software bug caused the electric motors to go into lock-down mode in the slowest parts of the circuit. With no electric power available to offset the turbo lag, nothing happened when the drivers pressed the throttle pedal. In Malaysia, the restrictions were lifted for the most problematic minisectors, with the FIA sending new software to the teams and manufacturers after approximately 20 minutes. They were then able to install the updated version in their power units to finally get the race under way. The same emergency measure was subsequently applied in Singapore, before a test with modified software followed in Austin. At the Circuit of the Americas, the FIA issued the following statement: "As part of the ongoing refinements to the Power Unit software for low grip mode, the FIA together with the teams and Power Unit manufacturers will run a simulation at the end of FP1, with cars running on low grip mode, using specific driver inputs during the in-lap to test additional software protections. This will mean that cars will be running for a short distance at low speed at Turn 15 at the end of the session." FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis had already explained in Malaysia that the bug had only come to light during the race because the FIA had not been able to carry out sufficient testing with the 2026 cars in wet conditions beforehand. In response to a question from Motorsport.com, he confirmed that he could guarantee this specific bug would not occur again, although he added that he could not rule out all bugs. Asked during the FIA press conference whether the drivers are confident that the Sepang debacle will not be repeated, Max Verstappen joked: "I have installed antivirus in my car, so I'll be fine!" item.title: WTA apologizes as recording aired of Pegula calling Andreeva a 'diva'
item.description: FILE PHOTO - US tennis player Jessica Pegula celebrates defeating Polish Iga Świątek during their women's singles final match of the Bad Homburg Open Tennis Tournament. (is associated with: «WTA apologizes as recording aired of Pegula calling Andreeva a 'diva'») Arne Dedert/dpa The WTA women's tennis tour has apologized and admitted it did not tell players their on-court conversations during practice sessions at the WTA Finals were being broadcast. A furore has broken out in Indian Wells after Jessica Pegula was heard on the WTA’s YouTube livestream making derogatory comments about Mirra Andreeva and her coach Conchita Martinez. A spokesperson for the governing body said on Thursday: “The WTA takes full responsibility for failing to inform our players and their teams that microphones, in place to give fans a livestream of the players’ practice, were active on the courts at the WTA Finals. “We sincerely apologize for failing to meet our responsibility to ensure players and coaches were properly informed.” The tour had intended for the microphones to capture ambient sounds from the court and has acknowledged it failed to ensure the appropriate safeguards were in place. A conversation between Pegula and her coach Mark Knowles has been widely scrutinized, with the US world number five critiquing the attitude of third-ranked Russian teenager Andreeva. Pegula can clearly be heard calling the 19-year-old a “diva” and saying she has lost respect for former Wimbledon champion Martinez for not calling out her behaviour. Pegula goes on to say Andreeva would be better than her fellow American Coco Gauff if she had the same mentality. Another practice session, meanwhile, saw world number one Elena Rybakina having an apparent spat with her coach. The WTA said it would continue to livestream practice sessions but without any audio. The WTA Finals, which features the best eight singles players and doubles teams of the year, begins on Sunday. Pegula and Andreeva have been drawn in different groups and cannot meet until the semi-finals. The incidents follow a debate at the Australian Open in January around the broadcasting of backstage areas, with Gauff annoyed after being filmed smashing her racket in what she thought was a private area. Gauff called for more privacy, while former world number one Iga Świątek said players were being treated like animals in a zoo.

And when the 2025 season began, it appeared to foster a major improvement in Jeff Hafley’s defense. In the first half of the 2025 season, Green Bay’s defense ranked 10th in DVOA and Parsons was on a tear. Through Week 15 of the 2025 season, he totaled 14 sacks and 79 pressures, looking every bit the force he had been with Dallas. Then, in Week 15 against the Denver Broncos, Parsons suffered a torn ACL, and things quickly fell apart for the Pack on Parsons’ side of the ball — and overall. The previously 9-3-1 Pack lost every game from then on, and their season ended abruptly with a 31-27 Wild Card playoff loss to the Chicago Bears. There wasn’t enough juice without their defensive epicenter to get things done. The Packers fell to 25th in Defensive DVOA in the second half of the season, and a primary reason was pretty clear. item.title: Donegal great Murphy retires from inter-county football
item.description: Murphy scored 1-4 in the 2012 All-Ireland final as Donegal beat Mayo to win the Sam Maguire [Getty Images] Donegal's All-Ireland winning captain Michael Murphy has announced his retirement from inter-county football for the second time. The 37-year-old made his Donegal debut in 2007 and captained the county to All-Ireland success in 2012, scoring 1-4 as they beat Mayo in the decider. The Glenswilly forward also won six Ulster Senior Football titles, including back-to-back triumphs in 2018 and 2019, and is a four-time All Star. He previously announced his inter-county retirement in 2022, but reversed the decision two years later and made a triumphant return under Jim McGuinness in the 2025 season. He helped his county to retain the Anglo-Celt Cup with an extra-time victory against Armagh and reach the All-Ireland final, which they lost to Kerry. His stellar performances earned him a fourth All-Star while he was also nominated for the Footballer of the Year award that year. Murphy stayed on for the 2026 season and while Donegal won the Division One title, his last game was their All-Ireland round-three exit to Dublin in June. "The Donegal County Board has today announced that former All-Ireland winning captain Michael Murphy has retired from inter-county football," the county said in a statement. "The player informed management in recent weeks once the club championship had concluded. "Michael has been Donegal's talisman for a generation and captained the county for most of his career having made his senior debut back in 2007. Two seasons ago, he came out of retirement, winning a sixth Ulster medal, his fourth All-Star and a national league title in the process." 'One of the giants of the modern game' Paying tribute to Murphy's decorated inter-county career, Donegal county board chairperson Mary Coughlan added: "Alas, we always knew this day would come but we are privileged to have watched the stellar career of Michael Murphy up close. "What he has given Donegal GAA on-and-off the field is simply extraordinary while always an ambassador par excellence and role-model for so many young people in our county and beyond. "He is one of the giants of the modern game and when players talk about leaving the jersey in a better place on retiring, Michael has certainly done that. He has carried himself with tremendous dignity and integrity at all times. "His innate modesty is a foil for a fierce competitor who never gave less than 100% while inspiring others around him to do likewise." Murphy's retirement is a further blow for boss McGuinness, who decided to remain at the helm for a fourth year in his second stint. He has also lost talented defender Finnbarr Roarty after the 2025 Young Footballer of the Year signed a two-year rookie contract with Aussie Rules outfit Collingwood.

item.title: Men’s Soccer: Northwestern stuns No. 13 Wisconsin in season closer
item.description: In their final matchup of the year the Wildcats (6-6-4, 3-4-3 B1G) closed out their season with a 3-1 win at home against No. 13 Wisconsin (10-3-4, 3-3-4 B1G), their second victory against a top-15 opponent this season. Entering the game, Northwestern was already out of the Big Ten Tournament due to its loss to Ohio State on Nov. 1, but Wisconsin still had hope, needing a win against the ‘Cats and some help from other teams to secure it a spot. However, the Wildcats quickly proved they weren’t going to give up a win easily, no matter how badly the Badgers wanted it. With a hat trick by senior Peter Riesz in his final game as a Wildcat, and six saves by goalie Dominic Pereira, the ‘Cats were able to come from behind and stun the Badgers and their tournament hopes, taking down Wisconsin for the first time since October 2021. Opening up the game, the Badgers were ready to start fast, as they recorded the first shot in the fourth minute, off the foot of Wilmette local Markie Hrvojevic, though the attempt missed the mark. From there, it remained quiet on shots until the 14th minute, when Wisconsin’s Emile Kisse shot wide of the goal after a diving tip by Pereira. From there it was back and forth between the teams, including a blast from NU’s Bryant Mayer that was saved. The continued stalemate between the two teams came to an end in the 33rd minute when Wisconsin got the first goal after an Aiden Martinez cross resulted in a Roman Eisa header, which found the back of the net, putting the No. 13 team up in the first half. Minutes later it seemed that the ‘Cats were able to tie the game up, only for the game-tying goal by Aaron O’Reilly to be called back due to a foul in the buildup. In the minutes before half, the ‘Cats had another opportunity to equalize when a corner from Tre Barrett almost found the net, but barely went over the goal. Going into the half, the red and white were up 1-0, having outshot the Wildcats 5-3. At the start of the second half, the Badgers maintained their momentum on goal. Wisco threatened the net, but the ’Cats kept them out of goal, with Pereira coming up with a huge point-blank save of Martinez. With the Badgers in striking distance, the Wildcats needed to strike and in the 58th minute they finally did that with a penalty kick following a Wisconsin foul inside the 18-yard box. It was Riesz who was able to crush the ball into the net and tie things up for the purple and white. As soon as the Wildcats scored, there was continued pressure from there, with three ‘Cats forcing saves out of Wisconsin just minutes later. Eventually, the continued pressure came to fruition, as the ‘Cats cashed in again in the 70th minute when Riesz smashed a right-footed attempt from 15 yards out with assists from Ethan Nakolo and Seth Mahlmeister. item.title: Nick Bosa says ‘I feel great’ and ‘I’m ready to go’
item.description: (Photo by Santiago Mejia/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) San Francisco 49ers star pass rusher Nick Bosa told reporters , “I feel great” and “I’m ready to go” on Wednesday. Bosa said it’s been tough, but he’s thinking more about the long haul. Bosa spoke about his injury: “It was my other leg. I must’ve had some type of compensation going on, especially in that first week back, just kind of trying to push it back with the tendonitis. So, I may have been favoring it a little bit. I was just doing my normal warm-up drills one day, and I tweaked it. Calves are a pretty long process. I’ve never had one, so it took a little longer than I expected. But I don’t even think about it anymore.” Bosa said the calf injury was unrelated to his Achilles. Bosa also mentioned how he could’ve returned earlier. General manager John Lynch was asked about the long-term strategy and plan for Bosa: We don’t take any game for granted, believe me. We only play 17 of these in the regular season, so they all count immensely. I think what we try to do in every situation is, we get our medical people, the doctors, the trainers, and the player involved. And we kinda look at these injuries from every angle involved, and we push ‘em to try to get them back. And when they’re ready, and there are a bunch of objective numbers to hit, to be able to do that. Nick saying that, he probably felt like he could, but I think all working together, we came to the decision that it was best to wait through Atlanta, to get the bye week and then come back. We’re happy we have him back. He’s obviously a difference maker when he’s out there. It will be great to have Nick out there on the field and making a difference like he always does. For as much talk as there is surrounding DeForest Buckner helping out the defensive tackles, Bosa takes immense pressure off Keion White and Romello Height to be every-down players and playing in situations you otherwise wouldn’t. The line will be fresh, but it will also have top-to-bottom talent we haven’t seen since 2022.

item.title: Miami’s High-Priced QB Loses Top Target Before Notre Dame Clash
item.description: In some ways, it’s hard for Miami’s Malachi Toney to describe how close he’s grown to Darian Mensah in a matter of months. The quarterback-wide receiver combination is one of the most potent 1-2 punches in college football this season and is the main reason why the Hurricanes are the No. 1 team in the initial College Football Playoff rankings released on Tuesday. “It’s just been crazy,” Toney told reporters this week. “We were just in the locker room just talking about how I saw him at [Prime 112 Restaurant] right after he committed. Just him getting adapted to Miami, we’ve grown so close.” That connection was disrupted Wednesday, when Toney suffered an ankle injury in practice and underwent surgery. He’s expected back later this season, but will miss Saturday’s much-anticipated matchup with Notre Dame, No. 11 in the Playoff rankings. But confidence remains high in Coral Gables because Miami has Mensah, who’s proven himself as a leader and competitor within Miami’s program since he arrived. “He’s eager to get the ball,” Miami head coach Mario Cristobal said this week. “Enthusiasm, excited, doesn’t flinch, very focused. Just ready, prepared. It was a preparation to give him that kind of confidence. He’s ready to roll.” Mensah has emerged as one of college football’s biggest stars this season. He’s at his third school in three years, having led Duke to a win in the ACC championship game in 2025 and Tulane to a 9-4 record in 2024. This year he’s been one of the most impactful transfer portal additions in the sport–Mensah leads the nation in touchdown passes (25), and his 80.7% completion percentage would break the NCAA single-season record by more than three points (Bo Nix, 77.4%, 2023). Overall, Miami’s offense leads the nation in scoring at 46.7 points per game. Mensah’s ascension encapsulates how player mobility has changed the sport. Each transfer has led to a bigger on-field opportunity and higher compensation. Mensah arrived at Tulane as a consensus three-star recruit in 2023. He signed a two-year, $8 million deal with Duke in 2024 , one of the biggest in college football at that time. Today, his $6.5 million NIL valuation at Miami is the highest in men’s collegiate athletics, according to On3 . Mensah’s endorsement deals include CVS, Derby Watch Supply, Dr. Pepper, and SlingTV. Saturday’s game at Notre Dame was the predetermined biggest game for Mensah and Miami this season, and Toney’s injury has scaled the challenge by a significant margin. Toney, like Mensah, is a nationwide leader in receiving; he ranks first in catches (73), receiving touchdowns (13), and is second in receiving yards (1,027). item.title: Rumor Makes NY Giants Trading For Derrick Henry Instead of Jonathan Taylor More Realistic Before Deadline
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect While the New York Giants are reportedly among the teams pursuing a Jonathan Taylor trade, a new rumor adds more steam to the idea that Derrick Henry is the more realistic trade addition before next week’s NFL trade deadline. The Giants are a team to watch over the next week. Heading into the Week 9 NFL schedule, they own a 4-2-1 record and sit atop the NFC East standings. A year ago, they were 2-5 and mentioned as potential sellers before the deadline. Now they have reasons to shop for upgrades to make a serious run at the division title in the second half. The rumblings around the team claim that, along with improving the interior of their defensive line, upgrading the backfield is a goal for the front office before Nov. 10. And according to reports over the weekend, the Giants are competing with the Minnesota Vikings , Green Bay Packers , Cincinnati Bengals , and Denver Broncos in the ongoing Taylor sweepstakes. Although ESPN’s Dan Graziano boldly claimed this week, “I would guess [Taylor] gets traded, and I wouldn’t be at all surprised if it was the Giants who made that move ” the reported asking price is a second-round pick and more, and that could rise if teams are desperate to add the three-time Pro Bowler. That is why the Giants must have alternative options on their wish list. Well, a new report from Jason La Canfora makes a move for the Baltimore Ravens RB make even more sense than his Indianapolis Colts counterpart. Derrick Henry trade may only cost New York Giants a third-round pick Oct 11, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry (22) runs during the fourth quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images According to the NFL insider, while some around the league believe Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta would be very hesitant to trade the five-time Pro Bowler, various executives “believe it is the only cogent path to start digging out of a massive roster, payroll, and salary cap hole and begin playing the youngsters on the roster.” Furthermore, one general manager told La Canfora that DeCosta “ could definitely get something for Henry, absolutely .” What would that something be exactly? With Henry having one more season left on his contract , “multiple executives” told the NFL insider that “the Ravens could get third-round value for Henry.” The Giants don’t have a fifth-round pick in 2027 , and their fourth-rounder is a compensatory. However, they do have a third-rounder. They could offer a third-rounder and a future Day 3 pick for Henry. Or try to blow the competition away and offer their second-round pick in 2027. DeCosta has to be willing to trade Henry first. However, Giants head coach John Harbaugh saw the value in the 32-year-old two years ago and pushed Baltimore to trade for him. He could see that same value now and get his old team on the phone and try to persuade them to make a deal over the next week.

item.title: England check on Palmer - what are Tuchel's other big choices?
item.description: Thomas Tuchel will name his next England squad on Friday [Getty Images] England have made medical checks on Cole Palmer as Thomas Tuchel considers whether to select the Chelsea forward in his next squad. The 24-year-old missed all four games during the previous international window with a minor injury. He completed 90 minutes for Chelsea against Brentford before those matches, and started for the Blues in the first game afterwards. Tuchel, who names his squad to face Croatia and Spain on Friday, said at the time that Palmer was "playing with discomfort and pain" but was "missing too many opportunities" with England. Whether he is recalled will be a key theme on Friday. While it is normal for England medics to check on players under consideration, it also underlines that Palmer remains on Tuchel's radar despite his stark comments last month. In addition to deciding whether to select Palmer, head coach Tuchel has a number of other dilemmas to resolve. Bukayo Saka's injury absence opens the door to another attacker, with his Arsenal team-mate Noni Madueke pushing for a recall following a string of impressive performances. Manchester United forward Marcus Rashford has not played since mid-October and is not fit for selection, while Chelsea defender Trevoh Chalobah is a major injury doubt. The likes of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice and many others are now stonewall selections - but the intrigue is around the remaining few spots still seemingly up for grabs. Scott and Ngumoha have already made their debuts for the senior side and Nwaneri is currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund. Tuchel said in his last press conference how King is close to a senior call-up and the midfielder has impressed for the under-21s too. item.title: NFL viewership stabilizes after early-season declines as league nears midway point
item.description: Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images After some viewership declines during the early portion of the season, the NFL is back on track. Entering Week 9, NFL viewership is up 3% year-over-year, according to a report by Austin Karp in Sports Business Journal . That increase is within the range that could be entirely attributed to Nielsen’s recent methodological changes that altered how the company measured co-viewing , the act of multiple people viewing one telecast in the same room. A recent report by The Athletic’s Stewart Mandel suggested Nielsen’s recent changes raised baseline college football viewership by 3.4% . It’s unclear if the NFL is seeing a similar lift, however. It’s important to note that the league came out publicly against Nielsen’s changes before the seas0n began. NFL telecasts are averaging 18.4 million viewers through Week 8. The two top audiences of the year both belong to the Kansas City Chiefs and CBS. Chiefs-Raiders averaged 28.45 million viewers on the network in October, and last weekend’s Chiefs-Broncos game averaged 28.18 million viewers. Fox holds the next two most-watched contests; Commanders-Cowboys in September (27.21 million viewers) and 49ers-Seahawks in October (26.70 million viewers). Per Karp, CBS is up 5% overall through Week 8, averaging 19.6 million viewers. Thursday Night Football on Prime Video also continues to trend up, averaging 17.6 million viewers per game. Each of its seven telecasts have seen year-over-year gains. ESPN’s Monday Night Football is up 22% versus last year, though it’s unclear if that number is buoyed by last year’s doubleheaders, which depressed ESPN’s per-game average and would make for a more favorable comparison. Figures for Fox’s and NBC’s viewership through Week 8 were not published. In data released to reporters on Thursday, the NFL pointed towards the number of close games as helping viewership this season. 71 games have been decided by one-score margins so far this season, tied with 2022 for the most in NFL history through eight weeks. 38 games have had a game-winning score in the final five minutes or overtime, tied with 2021 for the most through eight weeks. Closer games means higher viewership numbers. — Richard Deitsch (@richarddeitsch) November 5, 2026 Be it close games, Nielsen changes, or just normal viewership fluctuations, the league likes when ratings go up. And so far this season, the NFL continues to display its strength in viewership. item.description: Arsenal star told why he should consider Bundesliga move Martin Odegaard has been linked with a potential move to Bayern Munich , with the Arsenal captain being advised to consider joining the German giants if an opportunity arises. The Norwegian has established himself as one of the most important players in Mikel Arteta’s squad. item.title: Henry Cejudo, Kamaru Usman roast Colby Covington for embarrassing 43-second loss: ‘He’s supposed to beat Khamzat Chimaev?‘
item.description: Colby Covington | Chris Unger, Zuffa LLC Colby Covington lasted less than a minute against Raul Rosas Jr. and his peers are letting him have it. Rosas defeated Covington in a submission-only grappling match at a Hype Fighting event in Italy this past Tuesday, needing just 43 seconds to secure a rear-naked choke and force Covington to tap out. It was a stunning upset given Covington’s size advantage (Rosas typically competes at 135 pounds, Covington at 170) and experience as a former interim UFC champion. Longtime Covington rival Kamaru Usman broke down the loss alongside Pound 4 Pound co-host Henry Cejudo, who didn’t hold back with his criticism of Covington. “He gets f*cking taken down, double-legged, this is the whole fight, 40 seconds,” Cejudo said. “Look at this motherf*cker, and he’s supposed to beat Khamzat Chimaev next f*cking week?” Covington wrestles Khamzat Chimaev in the main event of RAF Abu Dhabi next Saturday. Given how Covington fared against a bantamweight, Cejudo is understandably skeptical of his chances against a former UFC middleweight champion. For Usman, who holds two title fight wins over Covington, he was surprised to see the wrestling-minded “Chaos” handled so easily. “First and foremost, I would say this: That’s not excusable because of your name and the brand that you’ve built,” Usman said. “It’s not excusable. Now us, real fighters and competitors, we know how difficult and how different they are. Super different. “Wrestling and jiu-jitsu are completely different. So Raul Rosas caught him off guard, got in there, and put him away.” Fortunately for Covington, the Hype Fighting event might have flew under the radar for the vast majority of fans, so he might receive less backlash than expected for such a disappointing performance. Still, Cejudo and Usman agree that the self-proclaimed “King of Miami” has to show up in his next RAF fight or the damage to his reputation could be far worse. “Colby Covington, you ain’t the king of shit no more,” Cejudo said, later adding, “This does hurt. I guess people will get over it. If he’s able to come out and beat Khamzat Chimaev, people will forget it, or maybe he’ll get a rematch with Raul Rosas, but I think Raul will probably do that shit again to him.” “You could see his face,” Usman said. “He was not ready for that level of intensity right away. For a guy that’s supposed to be intense, he was not ready for that level of intensity.”

item.description: Carlos Alcaraz’s steady return to fitness has belied his rapid return to form, which has been almost instant since he played his first competitive match back at the US Open in September. Since then, the Spaniard has already won two ATP titles and is currently into the quarter-finals of the Paris Masters . Given how ravaged the field in the French capital is, it feels like there is nobody left capable of stopping him from adding a new piece of silverware to his already sprawling cabinet. And yet, as he silently moves through the draw and closer to his first Paris Masters title, it is Jannik Sinner and Ben Shelton who have been dominating headlines. After all, their respective coaching changes both came as great surprises, and have sparked mass speculation about how Carlos Alcaraz might react. Brad Gilbert backs Carlos Alcaraz to make coaching change Speaking on the latest Big T podcast , it was Brad Gilbert who shared his theory for what the future might hold for Alcaraz. After all, since Juan Carlos Ferrero departed his team around this time last year, he has made no major additions to replace him, instead trusting in the guidance of Samu Lopez to spearhead his development. Discussing Ben Shelton ’s decision to add Alcaraz’s old coach to his team, Gilbert actually made a bold prediction about the seven-time Grand Slam champion, noting: “I’m sure he’s eager to get to work and make some changes so he can close the gap on Sinner, Alcaraz, and Zverev, and his combined record against the three is not that great. “But honestly, I do believe now after what Sinner did, you know… I expect at least two, three, more guys in the top ten to make big changes, and I expect two, three, women, probably, that are playing the year-end championships, to make changes. “I think, actually, Alcaraz will make a move soon, and the guy to keep most eyes on, I think, is David Ferrer. “Because he’s all of a sudden stopping as the Davis Cup captain. item.description: There was a sizable turnover between the roster and coaching staff from a year ago to now, many of which have no experience in the battle for the Paul Bunyan Trophy. One of those coaches is linebackers coach Alex Whittingham. On Wednesday with the media, he shared how all the new faces are learning about the intensity and physicality of the Michigan-Michigan State rivalry. “Mr. Jansen came in and he was great, gave us the whole background,” Whittingham said on Wednesday of Jon Jansen, former Michigan offensive lineman who spoke with the team this week. “I’ve been a college football fan for a while. That’s why I’m kind of familiar with it. I’m lucky to have been, you know, in the rivalries back in Utah, those games that they played the last eight years. I’ve seen NFL rivalries, which is a little different flavor to that. … So experience with rivalries and kind of how they work. Getting educated this week has been eye opening and good, and I’m very excited for this game.” An added bonus for Whittingham specifically is his room of linebackers has some unique experience with the rivalry. Graduate student Aisea Moa spent three years at BYU and then last season in East Lansing with Michigan State. Moa shared with the linebacker room what it was like to be on the other side of the rivalry. “We got Aisea Moa in the room, who is a Michigan State transfer, so he gives us an interesting perspective,” Whittingham said. “I had him speak to the guys in our linebacker room on Monday, just kind of give us a take on where they’re at on the other side and what they’re talking about. So that was good.” Just like any player, Whittingham has his fair share of experiences with rivalries. item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Leading up to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, the San Francisco 49ers are still being looked at as a team that could swing another deal. Of course, 49ers general manager John Lynch already added to the roster by trading a fourth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for DeForest Buckner. But there’s a sense that the 6-1 49ers might not be done. Interestingly enough, the latest 49ers trade rumor connects them to another All-Pro, but this time it’s at a position that’s already filled. Related: 1 Bold Prediction for Each Game in NFL Week 9, Including Bills-Vikings Could the San Francisco 49ers Trade for Jonathan Taylor? Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis in Week 6. Back in 2022, the 49ers paid a heavy price to trade for a First-Team All-Pro running back, trading a second, third, and fourth-round pick, plus a future fifth in exchange for Christian McCaffrey. Now four years later, could the 49ers’ front office be mulling a trade for another First-Team All-Pro RB? On Thursday’s edition of “ PFT Live ” Mike Florio and former NFL QB Chris Simms discussed the topic of Taylor’s trade market. According to Simms, some around the league have asked him whether the 49ers have any interest in trading for Taylor. Simms and 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan are good friends, so those inside league circles often wonder whether the NBC analyst has the inside scoop. “I’ve had a lot of people, insiders people from organizations text me, saying, ‘hey is your boy, do you think he’ll trade for Jonathan Taylor?’ Which, I have no idea about. But that conversation, people within the NFL certainly think there’s a possibility there, which would be shocking to me.” Chris Simms on Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors Like Taylor, McCaffrey is signed through the 2028 season, yet, CMC is also 30 years old. Yet, as Simms suggested, it would come as a “shock” if the 49ers once again ponied up and paid the price to trade for the top running back on the market. Yet, the 49ers clearly value having an excellent running game, and a 1-2 punch featuring McCaffrey and Taylor would definitely be the best in the NFL. Still, that doesn’t mean the 49ers will be the team that outbids others in pursuit of Taylor. Then again, it’s possible none of the teams meets the Colts asking price, which is believed to be similar to what the Carolina Panthers once got to trade McCaffrey. item.title: Valencia manager could field a five-man defence to stop Real Madrid in La Liga clash
item.description: Valencia manager could field a five-man defence to stop Real Madrid in La Liga clash Real Madrid are set to travel to Mestalla to face Valencia this weekend as they look to extend their winning streak to eight games. Jose Mourinho’s team are flying high on the confidence gained from their dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over AEK Athens . Los Blancos have proved to be an unstoppable attacking unit in recent weeks following some tactical tweaks from Jose Mourinho. Now, according to AS , Valencia manager Javier Aguirre is testing a five-man defence in training in an attempt to stop Real Madrid. Aguirre prepares a defensive reshuffle The Mexican manager has tested a back line consisting of Pablo Maffeo, Arnau Martinez, Pepelu, Cesar Tarrega and Jose Gaya. Arnau is said to be operating as the right-sided centre-back, while Maffeo and Gaya would occupy the wing-back positions. Valencia could field a five-man backline to stop Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Aguirre had already experimented with pairing Maffeo and Arnau against Elche, but the former operated in a much more advanced role. Against Real Madrid, though, Aguirre’s side will look to be as compact as possible defensively and prevent Los Blancos ‘ attackers from thriving. The proposed system is also said to feature Guido Rodriguez, Javi Guerra and youngster Aaron Mayol in midfield, with Arnaut Danjuma partnering Umar Sadiq in attack. The Nigerian recently scored Valencia’s winner against Elche and could return to the starting line-up against Madrid. A potential challenge for Real Madrid Valencia are always a difficult team to face at Mestalla , and they have become significantly more solid since Aguirre took over. This weekend would mark Real Madrid’s final league visit to the stadium, with Valencia set to move to a new stadium next season. Jose Mourinho’s men will face a stern test against Valencia at the Mestalla. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Aguirre’s approach appears designed to restrict Madrid’s attacking space, particularly in wide areas, while maintaining three central defenders to deal with Kylian Mbappe. For Mourinho’s men, breaking down such a deep block would require creativity and the likes of Arda Guler and Jude Bellingham to find a way through. With Vinicius Jr. still unavailable through suspension, Mourinho should have no problem playing the Turkish international against Valencia. A five-man defence would provide a new kind of challenge for Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, and it remains to be seen how they fare this weekend.

But the belief around the league is that, barring an offer that blows them away, Indianapolis plans to wait until after Sunday’s game vs the… https://t.co/R9AJq2MRRR pic.twitter.com/1p08ZP9gIi — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 5, 2026 There’s been some reported thought and speculation around the industry that the Colts potentially moved too quickly on trading two of their veteran pillars, Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner earlier last week, and did not possibly maximize the full trade return of either longtime organizational standout respectively. item.title: Lewis Hamilton backs claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than F1 rivals
item.description: Motorsport photo Lewis Hamilton maintains Ferrari needs further talks to iron out its rules of engagement, backing claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than drivers from rival teams. Hamilton and Leclerc came to blows on lap one of last weekend's race in Mexico with both drivers going off the track at Turn 4, which eventually handed Max Verstappen a golden opportunity to snatch away the win and costing Ferrari a possible 1-2 victory, instead the duo finishing second and fourth. Hamilton was incensed by how hard Leclerc raced on the opening lap, only for the Monegasque to permanently stay ahead as he cut the track at Turn 4. Leclerc only received a five-second penalty for gaining a lasting advantage, with mitigation bringing that punishment down from 10 seconds. Their Mexico fight further fed suggestions that Leclerc appears to race his teammate harder than anyone else, having come after a Singapore Grand Prix in which Leclerc backed off at the start despite being fully on the inside of polesitter Max Verstappen. Leclerc did race the Dutchman hard at the subsequent US Grand Prix in Austin, however, overtaking the Red Bull man around the outside of COTA's Esses. When asked if the idea of Leclerc racing him harder than other drivers is something Hamilton has also noticed, the seven-time world champion replied: "Yes. I see what you see. In Singapore, he was fully on the inside into Turn 1, he had won the lead, and he backed off. It was definitely different. "But I mean, if you look at the team-mates, it was the same with Sebastian [Vettel]. It was the same with Carlos [Sainz]. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari As emotions ran high, Hamilton demanded talks to clarify the team's rules of engagement and warned of "big problems" for the squad. Motorsport.com understands team principal Fred Vasseur has spoken briefly to both drivers, albeit separately, after feeling the events of Mexico showed a lack of respect towards the team's 2000 people staff. But with Vasseur having travelled back to Europe in between races and Leclerc spending time with his family following the birth of his daughter, Hamilton says further talks are still needed. "Naturally I was frustrated, and I'm still frustrated," he said when asked by Motorsport.com if he views the events of Mexico in a different light now they have had time to cool off. item.title: Joan Garcia opens up on adapting to Barcelona’s style: ‘I consider myself a very complete goalkeeper’
item.description: Joan Garcia opens up on adapting to Barcelona’s style: ‘I consider myself a very complete goalkeeper’ Being a goalkeeper for Barcelona is about more than just stopping shots. It is one of the most demanding roles in football. Playing in goal for Hansi Flick’s Barça is a whole other story. The goalkeeper must act as the last defender on a number of occasions and remain alert to the space behind the back line. Joan Garcia has embraced those responsibilities since arriving from Espanyol in 2025. He has emerged as the perfect goalkeeper for Flick’s Barcelona. More than a shot-stopper Speaking in an interview with GQ, the 25-year-old discussed his adaptation to Barcelona, his development as a goalkeeper and how he manages the pressure of representing the club. “I have always felt very comfortable helping the team in that aspect. It is true that at Barcelona it is much more necessary, and it is something I enjoy working on and practising to keep improving every day,” Garcia said. (h/t SPORT ). “I consider myself a very complete goalkeeper. I try to help in many aspects of the game and remain very alert to anticipate and prevent possible chances for the opposition,” he added. Joan Garcia kept his first clean sheet in the Champions League at Barcelona. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) These qualities are very valuable to Flick’s Barcelona. Joan has repeatedly timed his rushes off the line to perfection. He recently celebrated his first Champions League clean sheet for the Catalan club in Barcelona’s 3-0 victory over Aston Villa. Garcia on handling pressure and mental preparation The Spanish international has also spoken about the psychological demands of goalkeeping, where one mistake can define a player. “It is something we goalkeepers live with from a very young age. We know the position carries enormous responsibility, but it is not something that affects me too much,” he explained. “Over the years, I have learned to manage these situations much better and, at certain moments, I have worked with psychologists. At this elite level, I believe taking care of the mental side is fundamental.” Joan Garcia is slowly entering the scheme of things in the Spain squad. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Despite being only 25, Garcia also recognises his responsibility towards Barcelona’s younger players. “I try to contribute my experience, help and advise my teammates in whatever way I can, even though I am only 25 years old,” he said. The former Espanyol shot-stopper has also entered the reckoning for Spain under Luis de la Fuente, although a starting berth seems far-fetched. Joan Garcia has performed exceedingly well in the season and a half since he joined the club in 2025. It remains to be seen how the 25-year-old develops and whether he can be the goalkeeper who brings the Champions League back to the Spotify Camp Nou.

item.description: The opening ODI of India's upcoming home series against Sri Lanka has been shifted from Delhi to Visakhapatnam, with the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirming the venue change on Thursday. The December 13 fixture, originally scheduled to be played at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, will now take place at the ACA-VDCA Cricket Stadium in Visakhapatnam. Why has India vs Sri Lanka 1st ODI been shifted? The DDCA had approached the BCCI seeking a change in venue, citing its inability to host the international fixture amid renovation work and unfavourable weather conditions expected in Delhi during December. The association was concerned that the ongoing work at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, coupled with the possibility of weather-related disruptions, could affect the smooth organisation of the match. The BCCI subsequently approved the request and confirmed Visakhapatnam as the new venue for the series opener. item.title: 'Everyone wants an upset' - Martin's FA Cup warning
item.description: Russell Martin was appointed Leicester City boss on a three-year deal in the summer [Shutterstock] Leicester City manager Russell Martin has demanded his players do not give the people what they want on Friday – an FA Cup upset to savour. The 2021 competition winners and one-time Premier League champions travel to sixth-tier side Oxford City (19:45 GMT). With 64 places separating the two sides in the English football pyramid and the Foxes' stature as a club that conquered the Premier League against 5,000-1 odds just a decade ago, Martin does not shy away from what the tie represents. "Listen, we have been put on Friday night on TV for one reason - it's because everyone wants to see an upset, and that's what the FA Cup is about," he told BBC Radio Leicester. "It's about the underdog having the opportunity to have a brilliant day, to really have something to remember. "We have to avoid that. We have to really rise to the challenge, which is a different one, but we really have to show how much we've grown as a team." Is Leicester boss Martin turning the Foxes' fortunes? Leicester assistant Hourihane leaves after four months Leicester held at home by Stevenage Martin's Foxes have endured a slow start on their return to the third tier for just the second time in the club's 142-year history, winning five and losing four of their 13 League One games so far. Defeats by Robbie Savage's Peterborough United, a 4-0 drubbing by Oxford United and 2-1 loss at Burton Albion has left the former Rangers, Southampton and Swansea City boss to deal with significant scrutiny a number of times in the early months of his tenure. As the boss that was brought in to revive Leicester after back-to-back relegations from the Premier League and Championship, a 'cupset' now would only ramp up the pressure more. For that reason, and Martin's own history as a player, he is not about to rotate his side of experiment against the National League North hosts. "Definitely not - it's a game we want to win and we'll go as strong as we possibly can," he said. Early in his career Martin was part of the Peterborough United side that took then Premier League club West Bromwich Albion to a replay in 2009. A few years later he was Norwich City captain when the then top-flight side were knocked out by then non-league Luton Town. "I've been with a lower league team and the underdog and gone to Premier League teams and loved it, but I've also been a player in a Premier League team and got beat by a Conference team at Norwich," he said.
